target_customer: B2B sales teams that buy warm introductions; individuals with large networks earn the bounty
problem: Cold outreach converts poorly, and people with valuable networks have no way to monetize introductions.
business_model: Marketplace with per-introduction bounty (average reported as $500)

technical_complexity.rationale: Marketplace and network graph from relationship signals; mostly standard web engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Two sided connector and buyer network could be a moat, but it was early and copied easily by similar tools.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbent action; not established.

market_need_then: Company reports hundreds of paying companies within weeks of its February 2024 launch and 97 percent inbound or word of mouth; these are self-reported.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand coverage found. The name is descriptive of partnerships and similar to PartnerStack and others in search results.

outcome_analysis: PartnerHQ is a Winter 2024 company that launched in February 2024 and reports hundreds of paying customers and a 97 percent inbound user base, all self-reported. No funding beyond YC was verified and no exit or failure signal exists, so the story is too early to attribute to specific success or failure factors.
notes: UNVERIFIED: aggregators say $500K seed (April 2024) from Y Combinator, Eight Capital, Rebel Fund and others, and disagree on investors and stage; not entered as a round. Brackets For Good claim and Stanford education come from low quality pages. Competition left empty: the competitor pages found are dated 2026. Company site not fetched. Completeness pass: the $500K round (2024-04) rests on aggregators (VCBacked, Standout) with no primary source; stage is pre-seed per VCBacked and seed per Standout, and other profiles name different investors.
